# Objective

Apply the five verified second-round review findings (plus the symmetric
lead-clip gap found during evaluation and a temp-registration leak found
during implementation) as one fix batch, keeping the suite green and the
documented policies in sync.

# Verified findings (all reproduced before fixing)

1. `record.remove_tag()` does not exist in pysam 0.24.1 — any moved read
   carrying a stale aligner tag (BWA tags `AS` on every primary) aborts the
   run with `AttributeError`.
2. Under `--force`, a failure between publications destroys previously
   existing outputs: `os.replace` clobbers them and rollback deletes the
   replacements without restoring the originals.
3. Equal aligned ends always selected struct1 as the trailing-clip owner, so
   a colocated `20M` + `20M5S` pair merged to `20M`, losing R2's 5 outer
   bases (regression from the first fix batch). The lead owner had the
   mirrored latent bug on equal starts.
4. Templates with only secondary/supplementary records hit
   `assert record is not None` and exited 1, contradicting the documented
   pass-through policy.
5. `_both_mapped` fetched the whole span between distant mates before the
   fragment-length rejection (measured 100,020 bases for zero overlap).

# Changes as executed

- `src/pairloom/merge.py`: `_lead_owner`/`_trail_owner` helpers — aligned
  extent first, then the longer clip on equal coordinates (deterministic
  struct1 on a full tie); module docstring updated.
- `src/pairloom/pipeline.py`:
  - stale-tag removal via `set_tag(tag, None)` with a comment pinning the
    pysam API fact;
  - publish loop moves existing outputs aside (`.pairloom-bak-<pid>`),
    deletes backups on success; `_rollback` restores them on failure;
    sorted/index temps registered for cleanup;
  - primary-less templates classify `neither_aligned` and pass through
    untagged (documented §15-style default);
  - overlap analysis fetches only the aligned-span intersection, skipped
    entirely when empty.
- Tests: 7 regressions added — tagged-move and bounded-fetch
  (test_integration), publish-restore under a one-shot injected failure
  (test_errors), three clip-tie cases (test_merge), secondary-only
  pass-through in both modes (test_classify_policy). Suite 130 → 137.
- README: primary-less record policy, clip tie rule, publish integrity
  under `--force`, intersection-only fetch in the memory paragraph, test
  count.

# Steps actually taken

1. Plan written; all five findings re-verified (pysam API check plus the
   evaluation turn's reproduction script).
2. Fixes 3 (merge.py) then 1/4/5/2 (pipeline.py); suite green after each
   step.
3. Regression tests added; the publish-restore test initially failed
   because its injection also blocked the rollback's restore move (same
   destination path) — corrected to a one-shot failure, which is the
   realistic scenario anyway.
4. ruff format applied to two test files; full gates re-run.
5. Reproduction script re-run at the original bug sites: all five behaviors
   corrected; benchmark re-measured (unchanged).

# Verification

- `pixi run test`: 137 passed (was 130; +7 regressions).
- Reproduction re-run: tagged pair exits 0 with tags removed; injected
  publish failure restores prior outputs; `20M5S` tie correct;
  secondary-only template exits 0 as `neither_aligned`; max fetch 1,020
  bases (was 100,020).
- `pixi run lint` / `pixi run format`: clean.
- Benchmark: 1 thread 7.6 s / 2,643 pairs/s / 224 MiB — unchanged.

# Risks encountered

- The publish-failure injection taught the rollback constraint the hard
  way: restore moves share destination paths with publications, so failure
  injection in tests must be one-shot.
- Report and audit validators each rejected one item (structure/length);
  corrected to the exact schema.
